A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same work, with matching methods and main experiments. v1 ends after the references; v2 adds supplementary Section 6. The supplied text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original automatic evaluations on Ego-Exo4D and LEMMA, human preference studies, and component ablations in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds supplementary ablations, feature analyses, pseudo-label statistics and reduced-camera evaluation.

M1.justification: The caption-based pseudo-labeler, rank aggregation, TimeSformer view selector, auxiliary pose predictor and training losses remain unchanged. Section 6.8 supplies implementation details; the supplementary ablation variants do not replace the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both datasets and their activity coverage are retained. Section 6.6 adds an Ego-Exo4D scenario with one ego and one exo candidate view, extending reduced-camera evaluation to its diverse physical and procedural activities.

E2.justification: The main baseline and human-study comparator sets are unchanged. Table 7's Ego and Pixel-objectness match Ego-only and Snap angles. Table 4 adds two comparison variants beyond the existing ablations: frozen captioners and exact camera-displacement prediction.

E3.justification: New supplementary protocols evaluate every ego/exo pair and average their metrics, compare best/second-best/worst ranked selections, and introduce frozen-captioner and exact-displacement controls. The original metrics and human-study settings remain unchanged. Newly documented preprocessing and optimization settings do not establish changes to existing experiments.

E4.justification: Sections 6.2–6.6 substantially expand the original component ablations and failure examples. Additions test captioner fine-tuning, direction versus exact-displacement prediction, feature separation with and without pose supervision, selection rank, pseudo-label distributions, and robustness to fewer cameras.

E5.justification: Both versions report significance using p ≤ 0.05 without specifying the statistical test, repeated-run counts, seeds or confidence intervals. The supplementary tables extend the same reporting practice; preprocessing standard deviations are not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their numerical values. Tables 4–7 add substantial results, including CIDEr 0.4 without captioner fine-tuning versus 13.5 for the full model, and 12.7 for Ours versus 11.5 for Hand-object in the new single-exo setting. Ranking, feature and pseudo-label findings are also added. These are additional comparisons, not same-setting performance changes between versions.

T1.justification: The formal task definition, pose formulation and losses in Equations (1)–(2) remain equivalent. The supplement adds empirical analyses and implementation specifications, with no new theorem, proof or substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: language-based weak supervision without best-view labels, auxiliary pose supervision, video-only inference, and superior automatic and human evaluation results on two datasets.

C2.justification: The supplement adds interpretations concerning the inadequacy of frozen generic captioners, correspondence between learned ranking and view quality, and dataset-dependent pseudo-label preferences. These refine the existing explanation of viewpoint sensitivity. The narration-related failure condition remains represented in Figure 3 despite shortened prose.

D1.justification: Sections 6.7–6.8 add frame sampling, resizing and normalization, clip construction, narration processing, captioner prompts and frozen modules, detailed network layers, optimizer schedules, batch sizes and stopping criteria. They also explain Snap angles implementation and add project/video access information. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation without establishing an implementation change.

R1.justification: Twelve cited works are added, chiefly supporting supplementary implementation and analysis, including ViT, LoRA, AdamW, batch normalization, t-SNE and narration-based preprocessing. The related-work discussion and positioning against previous view-selection research remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section order and most prose are retained. Changes include localized terminology, grammar and caption edits, supplementary cross-references, and the organized addition of Section 6. There is no extensive rewriting or reorganization of the existing narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4–7 and Figures 4–6, providing ablation and ranking displays, paired t-SNE plots, pseudo-label distributions and expanded qualitative examples. Some examples reuse previously shown scenes with additional caption/rank information. Existing figures and tables are retained with sizing, spacing and caption adjustments.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially reduces v1's implementation-documentation gaps through Sections 6.7–6.8 and adds targeted evidence about fine-tuning, pose supervision and learned view ranking. These improve reproducibility and support for the method while preserving the original results. Table 7's unexplained all-zero Longest-caption row and unchanged sparse significance reporting limit the supplementary evidence, but do not outweigh the substantial documentation and diagnostic gains.
